'''''Allamanda cathartica''''', commonly called '''golden trumpet''',<ref name=GRIN>{{GRIN | accessdate=2 September 2014}}</ref> '''common trumpetvine''',<ref name=GRIN/> and '''yellow allamanda''',<ref name=GRIN/> is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Apocynaceae]]. It is native to [[Bolivia]], [[Brazil]], [[French Guiana]], [[Guyana]], [[Suriname]], and [[Venezuela]], and widely [[naturalisation (biology)|naturalised]] elsewhere in the tropics.<ref name="POWO">{{cite web | title=Plants of the World Online | website=Plants of the World Online | date=2020-07-16 | url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:319065-2 | access-date=2025-06-11}}</ref> This plant is cited in ''[[Flora Brasiliensis]]'' by [[Carl Friedrich Philipp von Martius]].

It does not twine, nor does it have [[tendril]]s or aerial roots. It can be pruned into a [[shrub]] form. If not pruned it can sprawl to a height of {{cvt|6|m}}.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gardenguides.com/98570-golden-trumpet-plant.html#ixzz1OvuMi9Pp |title=Golden Trumpet Plant |publisher=Garden Guides |date= |accessdate=2012-07-06}}</ref>{{Failed verification|reason=Cited source says it does twine, and doesn't mention pruning|date=November 2024}} According to McMullen, it can be up to {{cvt|15|m}} in length in the [[Galapagos Islands]] where it is naturalised.<ref>{{cite book | last= McMullen | first= Conley K. | date= 1999 |title= Flowering Plants of the Galapagos | location= Ithaca, N.Y. | publisher= Comstock Publishing Associates | page= 318 | ISBN= 0-8014-8621-1}}</ref>

The city of [[Canóvanas, Puerto Rico]] has adopted this species, known locally as ''canario amarillo'', as its official flower.<ref>[http://www.canovanas.pr/Datos-de-Interes/Simbolos.aspx Símbolos Oficiales.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140822225733/http://www.canovanas.pr/Datos-de-Interes/Simbolos.aspx |date=2014-08-22 }} Municipio de Canóvanas.</ref>[[File:Allamanda cathartica pic001.jpg|thumb|Allamanda cathartica flower at Tagore park Mahe district of Puducherry UT, India]]

==Cultivation==
The species is cultivated as a house plant. It requires a soil rich in organic matter, temperatures of not less than {{convert|18|C}} during the growing season, plenty of moisture, and bright light but not direct sunlight. During the rest season from October to March, the plant should be watered more sparingly and can endure temperatures down to {{convert|13|C}}. It should be repotted every year until it is in a container of {{cvt|40|–|50|cm}}. Propagation is by cuttings taken from April to May.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Chiusoli |first1=Alessandro |last2=Boriani |first2=Luisa Maria |title=Simon & Schuster's guide to houseplants |date=1986 |publisher=Simon and Schuster |location=New York |isbn=0671631314}}</ref>
